Corollary
[Calderon--Zygmund estimate for Poisson's equation] 1. ch9:9.10\group chapter-9Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0247 If $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^n$, $u\in W^{2,p}_0(\Omega )$, and $1<p<\infty $, then \begin{equation} \tag {9.33} \| D^2u\| _p\le C(n,p)\| \Delta u\| _p. \end{equation} For $p=2$, \begin{equation} \tag {9.34} \| D^2u\| _2=\| \Delta u\| _2. \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch Extend $\Delta u$ by zero and apply Theorem 25 to its Newtonian potential. The difference from $u$ is harmonic with zero Sobolev trace, hence vanishes; density treats general $u$.

□
